title: Spain Pick & Roll
description: A standard pick-and-roll with a back screen on the roller's defender — the action that broke modern defenses.
whatIsIt: Spain pick-and-roll starts like any ball screen — then adds a twist: as the screener rolls, a third offensive player sets a back screen on the roller's defender. That back screen is what makes it 'Spain.'

The genius is in the conflict it creates. The roller's defender is taught to tag the roll or help on the ball — but now someone is screening their back. If they help, the back screener's man is open; if they stay, the roller is open; if the defense switches everything, mismatches appear everywhere.
Named after the Spanish national team that popularized it internationally, Spain PNR is now a staple of NBA and EuroLeague offenses — and the ultimate test of a defense's communication.
whyItMatters: Spain PNR attacks the exact defender every coverage relies on: the roller's defender, the one who tags, helps, or drops. By screening that player, the offense removes the defense's safety net. It is the most efficient half-court action in modern basketball because it creates a good shot against almost any coverage.

howTo.title: Start a normal side pick-and-roll
howTo.detail: Ball handler and screener run a standard side PNR. Everything must look ordinary — the surprise is the point.

howTo.title: Time the back screen
howTo.detail: As the screener rolls, the third player (often in the opposite corner or slot) sprints up to set a back screen on the roller's defender. Timing is everything — too early and the defense sees it, too late and the roller is already tagged.

howTo.title: Read the roller's defender
howTo.detail: If they fight through the back screen, the roller is open at the rim. If they get stuck, the back screener pops or slips for their own shot.

howTo.title: Ball handler: attack the chaos
howTo.detail: With the middle of the defense screened, drive or pull up. The defense is now guarding three threats with two and a half defenders.

howTo.title: Have a counter for the switch
howTo.detail: If the defense switches the back screen, the back screener's defender is now on the roller — usually a mismatch. Feed the post or re-screen.

howTo.title: Space the weak side
howTo.detail: The two uninvolved players must hold the defense honest — corners filled, ready to shoot. Their gravity is what keeps help from arriving.

coachingPoints: Teach it 3v3 first: ball handler, roller, back screener vs three defenders. Add the other two later.
The back screen must be legal and physical — a soft back screen gets slipped and the action dies.
Timing reps are non-negotiable: run it until the back screener arrives exactly as the roll develops.
Teach all three reads (roller, back screener, ball handler) — players tend to only see their own.
commonMistakes: Setting the back screen too early, letting the defense call it out and switch cleanly.
The back screener screening air because the roller's defender already helped elsewhere.
Forgetting weak-side spacing, so a third defender helps and kills the advantage.
Running it with players who can't make the reads — Spain PNR punishes low-IQ lineups.
gameSituations: Against drop coverage, where the back screen removes the drop big from the play.
When the defense tags the roller aggressively — the back screen is the direct counter.
Late-game or ATO (after timeout) when you need one high-efficiency look.
